extra_misconceptions.fact: Pressing wrists against a pad while typing compresses the carpal tunnel; float your wrists neutral and use rests only during pauses.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Resting your wrists firmly on a padded gel wrist rest while actively typing prevents carpal tunnel syndrome and tendon strain.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Forceful stretching irritates inflamed tendons; stop typing right away, rest the hand in a neutral position, and apply a cold pack.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Typing harder and stretching aching fingers backward immediately relieves tendon inflammation during a long programming session.

extra_misconceptions.fact: High screen glare against a dark room forces your pupils to adjust constantly; match screen brightness to even ambient room lighting.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Sitting close to a bright monitor in a dark room sharpens text contrast and reduces eye fatigue during late-night coding.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Full screenshots often leak API keys, local file paths, browser tabs, or personal data that should be cropped or redacted first.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Sharing a screenshot of your full desktop or code editor online is safe as long as no password box is open on screen.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to the median nerve inside your wrist when you type for hours with your wrists bent upward on a desk edge?
Where should a Scout position the top of the monitor screen and set the viewing distance to prevent neck and eye strain?
Which physical indicator in your fingers or forearm warns of early repetitive stress injury before steady pain develops?
What measurement confirms that you are following the 20-20-20 rule properly during a long coding session at your desk?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Lovelace wrote her Bernoulli number algorithm in 1843 for Charles Babbage's mechanical Analytical Engine, which was never completed.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Ada Lovelace wrote the first computer program by testing her code directly on a running electronic computer in the 1840s.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Processors execute only binary machine instructions, so a compiler or interpreter must translate high-level code before it can run.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: High-level languages like FORTRAN and COBOL run directly on the processor without being translated into machine code first.

extra_misconceptions.fact: In 1947, operators taped an actual moth into the Harvard Mark II logbook after removing it from a relay that caused a malfunction.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Grace Hopper invented the term debugging purely as a metaphor because early computer programs had no actual physical hardware bugs.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Object-oriented concepts originated in the 1960s with Simula 67 and matured in the 1970s with Smalltalk long before the World Wide Web.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Object-oriented programming was invented in the 1990s specifically to build interactive web pages with Java and JavaScript.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to software portability when a programmer switches from hardware-specific assembly code to a compiled language?
Under what condition does an interpreter execute source code differently than a compiler such as Grace Hopper's A-0 system?
Which physical indicator on a torn or mispunched Hollerith card caused early mainframe batch programs to halt or misread data?
Why did early scientific programmers adopt FORTRAN in 1957 instead of writing raw binary machine instructions by hand?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Java is a statically typed language compiled to bytecode, while JavaScript is a dynamic scripting language created for web interactivity.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Java and JavaScript are two versions of the same programming language designed by the same engineering team for web browsers.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Modern appliances contain embedded microcontrollers running C or assembly firmware that read sensors, update displays, and time cycles.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Everyday household appliances like microwave ovens and washing machines operate purely on analog timers without programmed code.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Pure Python is relatively slow, so libraries like NumPy and PyTorch delegate heavy matrix math to compiled C, C++, and CUDA kernels.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Python is the fastest language for raw CPU number crunching because it dominates data science and machine learning workflows.

extra_misconceptions.fact: SQL is a domain-specific query language built to define, retrieve, and update relational database records rather than render graphics.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: SQL is a general-purpose programming language used to build mobile user interfaces and 3D game physics engines from scratch.

extra_socratic_questions: Under what condition does an automotive engineer choose C or C++ over Python for an anti-lock braking microcontroller?
What happens to a web application's database when backend code runs raw user input instead of parameterized SQL queries?
Which physical indicator or sensor input triggers a smart thermostat's embedded firmware to cycle a home heating relay?
What measurement confirms whether an embedded device has enough RAM and flash memory to run a managed language runtime?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Retail software purchases grant a conditional license to use the program under EULA terms while the publisher retains ownership.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Buying a commercial video game or desktop program makes you the legal owner of the software code with full rights to resell copies.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Freeware is free of charge but usually keeps its source code closed, whereas open-source software grants rights to inspect and modify code.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Freeware and open-source software mean the exact same thing because neither requires the user to pay money to download it.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Copyright attaches automatically upon creation, so public repositories without a license reserve all rights to the original author.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Any source code posted publicly on GitHub without a license file is automatically in the public domain for anyone to reuse.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Copyright protects the specific expression of source code, while only a utility patent can restrict others from implementing the method.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Copyright law prevents another programmer from writing fresh original code that performs the exact same task as your program.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to your legal rights when you click agree on an End User License Agreement after paying for a software download?
Under what condition does a company lose trade secret protection over a proprietary search or compression algorithm?
Why is it dangerous to copy a function from a GPL open-source repository into a closed-source commercial app without checking?
Which legal protection covers a software product's brand name and logo rather than its underlying source code or invention?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Logic bugs and off-by-one errors compile cleanly, so you must test normal, boundary, and invalid inputs to verify correct behavior.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A program that compiles and runs without throwing an error message is guaranteed to produce accurate output for every user input.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Editing multiple variables at once masks the true cause; change one thing at a time and re-run your test case to confirm the fix.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Changing five or six lines of code at once is the fastest way to isolate and fix a stubborn bug during a debugging session.

extra_misconceptions.fact: An IDE is just a workspace combining a text editor, debugger, and build runner; the actual language is defined by its compiler or runtime.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: An Integrated Development Environment is the programming language itself rather than a tool suite for editing and running code.

extra_misconceptions.fact: A valid program must read live input into variables, apply conditional or mathematical logic, and compute the resulting output dynamically.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Hardcoding the sample answer directly into a print statement satisfies the requirement to process user input and produce output.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to a Python program when you pass a user string directly from the input function into an arithmetic calculation?
Where should a Scout place a debugger breakpoint when a loop outputs the wrong total only on the final iteration?
Under what condition does a program compile with zero syntax errors in your IDE yet still crash or print wrong results?
What test input confirms that your conditional logic handles boundary values, zero, and unexpected negative numbers safely?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Engineers spend much of their week reading existing code, debugging systems, writing design docs, and reviewing changes with teammates.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Professional software engineers spend forty hours a week working alone in silence writing brand-new code from scratch.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Employers value problem-solving, version control habits, and debugging skills because developers look up API syntax details every day.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Memorizing every function in a language reference manual is required before you can qualify for an entry-level coding job.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Most technology companies offer parallel individual contributor tracks such as Staff and Principal Engineer focused on technical leadership.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Career advancement in software engineering always requires giving up programming to become a full-time people manager.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Hobbyists regularly write code for robotics competitions, amateur radio, home weather stations, music synthesis, and game modding.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Only full-time software company employees use programming skills, leaving little room for coding in outdoor or creative hobbies.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to a software team's release schedule when engineers only write code and skip code reviews and automated testing?
Which portfolio artifact demonstrates your real programming skill to a hiring manager better than listing languages on a resume?
Under what condition does an entry-level developer benefit more from contributing to an open-source project than taking a course?
What measurement confirms whether a computer science degree or a coding bootcamp offers a better return on tuition cost?
